text:
Maya Patel: Heads-up — terraform apply for a new gpu nodegroup in eu-west-1 (k8s-cluster-prod) failed during IAM setup. Apply aborted. Anyone seen this pattern today?
Jack Liu: what error did you get? can you paste the last lines?
Maya Patel: 
```
Error: Error creating IAM Role Policy Attachment: NoSuchEntity: The role with name 'k8s-nodegroup-role-prod' cannot be found
	status code: 404, request id: 9f2e...
```
Maya Patel: plan looked fine earlier, apply failed when attaching policies — role appears to have been created in the same run but attach fails.
Priya Rao: sounds like eventual consistency on IAM. If role creation and attachment happen in parallel within the same apply we sometimes hit this. Which module/version? are we using aws_iam_role_policy_attachment resource (non-deprecated) or the newer inline policy pattern?
Maya Patel: module is our fork of terraform-aws-nodegroup v3.2. We create the role in the module and then attachments also in the module. Also noticed ArgoCD sync for the cluster-addon helm chart got stuck around the same time.
Sam Ortega: ArgoCD reported an error for the addon app — it failed to apply a ServiceAccount because the annotation referenced a role ARN that didn't exist yet. Helm rendered the SA with `eks.amazonaws.com/role-arn: <arn>` so the admission webhook (eks-iam) rejected it.
InfraBot: deploy-bot: ArgoCD sync failed for app/cluster-addons (commit abc123): unable to apply ServiceAccount "cluster-addon-sa": admission webhook denied: referenced IAM role not found.
Jack Liu: short-term fix — create the IAM role manually (aws iam create-role) then re-run terraform, or use `terraform apply -target=module.nodegroup.module.iam_role` first then apply the rest. Also a `null_resource` with a simple aws cli describe-role + retry can gate the attach step.
Priya Rao: agree. For long-term we should split role creation out so it's not in the same transactional graph as attachments + nodegroup. I'll open a PR to separate iam module outputs and add explicit depends_on from nodegroup -> iam role. Also add a preflight job in our GitOps pipeline that waits for role propagation.
Maya Patel: attaching failed plan snippet and the tfstate excerpt in the ticket I opened: https://internal-tfstate/reports/1824005123 (link in thread). I've paused the rollout so no more partial nodegroups spin up.
Sam Ortega: Note for canary: if we re-create nodegroup after manual fix, confirm instance provisioning type — avoid mass spot allocation during retries. Set maxUnavailable low for the canary call. Also check quota in eu-west-1 GPUs (we're near soft limit).
Priya Rao: good catch on quotas. I'll add a quick quota check to the preflight job. For the GitOps flow I'll: 1) split IAM role into dedicated module, 2) add `aws iam get-role` retry in a CI step, 3) add Helm tolerance for missing SA during initial create (small patch), and 4) add a note about AWS eventual-consistency in the module README.
Jack Liu: if this becomes frequent we should also consider giving the role a deterministic name and provisioning it via an account-level bootstrap so nodegroup provisioning doesn't rely on same-run resources.
Maya Patel: thanks — assigning to @Priya to own the PR. I'll re-run the apply once PR lands and CI preflight passes. :thumbsup:
Priya Rao: will do, pushing draft in ~30m. I'll also add a short blameless incident note for the oncall queue so infra knows to expect this during nodegroup rollouts.
Sam Ortega: leaving a reminder to check cost impact if we end up re-running provisioning repeatedly — ops-costs channel should be notified if retries exceed threshold.
Maya Patel: cool, thanks everyone. I'll post results after the PR and a manual role creation test. :white_check_mark:
